tagline: Free Android calorie counter and weight tracker that looks up foods in Open Food Facts and USDA data.
description: Waistline is a mobile app, not a server. It runs on Android, is built with Cordova and the Framework7 library, and keeps its data on the phone. There is nothing to host: you install the app from F-Droid or Google Play and back up its data yourself. The diary records what you eat across the day. The food list is a local database you fill by typing foods in, scanning a barcode or searching online. Online lookups use Open Food Facts and the USDA food database, and only the barcode or search term leaves the phone. The app can import and export its data for backups and restores. It has no advertising and no in-app purchases. The README says it works on Android 5.0 and later. The licence is GPLv3. It replaces the logging side of paid calorie apps such as MyFitnessPal Premium. A community project offers a French food database based on ANSES-CIQUAL open data for people outside the US.
strengths: No ads and no in-app purchases
Looks up products by barcode scan or text search in Open Food Facts and the USDA database
Data stays on the phone, and the README says no personal data is collected
Import and export of app data for backup and restore
Distributed through F-Droid as well as Google Play
limits: Android only, with no iOS app and no web version
Nothing is hosted or synced between devices, so moving to a new phone relies on manual export and import
Online food data comes from Open Food Facts and the USDA, so coverage depends on those open databases
Camera and storage permissions are needed for barcode scanning and for import and export
bestFor: An Android user who wants to log calories and weight privately, without a subscription or an account.
